selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What is the main message of this passage about Allah?
questions.answer: It teaches that Allah alone is the only true God, and many signs in the universe show His oneness.

questions.question: Why is Allah’s greatness mentioned as a proof of His unity?
questions.answer: Because such complete greatness and all-reaching majesty belong to only one Lord.

questions.question: What does the passage say about the way Allah’s actions appear?
questions.answer: They appear in a complete and endless way, under His will and wisdom.

questions.question: What is one proof taken from Allah’s actions?
questions.answer: His actions are limitless yet always controlled by wisdom and will.

questions.question: Why are the Divine Names important in this passage?
questions.answer: They show that the same Lord’s qualities are active throughout the universe.

questions.question: What does the passage teach by describing beings as connected and mixed within one whole?
questions.answer: It teaches that creation belongs to one united system.

questions.question: Why does universal order argue against partners being joined with Allah?
questions.answer: Because one complete order across everything points to one ruler, not many.

questions.question: What is special about the elements and living kinds on earth in this passage?
questions.answer: They are spread widely and strongly over the earth, yet they still point back to one Lord.

questions.question: Why does the passage mention both Names and deeds together?
questions.answer: Because Allah’s qualities and actions both appear in a united way throughout creation.

questions.question: What short statement at the end sums up the lesson of the whole passage?
questions.answer: Everything contains a sign that points to Allah’s oneness.

questions.question: What belief is repeated at the beginning of the target passage?
questions.answer: That there is no god but Allah, the One and Unique.

questions.question: How many main truths are mentioned in this short summary?
questions.answer: Five main truths are mentioned.

questions.question: What is one proof taken from Allah’s greatness?
questions.answer: His complete majesty and vast perfection point to one unmatched Lord.

questions.question: How can one order cover the whole universe unless its Maker is one?
questions.answer: It could not fully do so, because complete order across all things needs one ruler.

questions.question: Why is it important that many things are made with ease and beauty?
questions.answer: Because that kind of creation shows perfect power and skill from one Creator.

questions.question: What does it mean that beings are joined and connected?
questions.answer: It means creation fits together in a wide, linked, and meaningful way.

questions.question: What are “Names and deeds” in this passage meant to show?
questions.answer: They show Allah’s qualities and actions working throughout the universe as one.

questions.question: What does the unity of cosmic management point to?
questions.answer: It points to the oneness of the Maker.

questions.question: What is one proof taken from the earth’s elements and species?
questions.answer: Their wide spread over the earth still follows one command.

questions.question: According to the final line, where can a person find a sign of Allah’s unity?
questions.answer: In every single thing.

questions.question: At this stopping-place, what is the traveler studying in the world?
questions.answer: Signs that prove the unity of Allah.

questions.question: Does the passage give only one proof or many proofs for Allah’s unity?
questions.answer: It gives many proofs.

questions.question: What does the passage mean by saying beings are interrelated?
questions.answer: It means they are tied to one another in a meaningful system.

questions.question: What does the unrestricted appearance of deeds tell us?
questions.answer: It tells us Allah acts freely and fully, while always with wisdom and will.
